en: 50 g oats
200 ml low-fat milk
1 apple, grated
1 tsp honey, cinnamon
A small knob of butter (optional)
Cook the oats with the milk over low heat 7 minutes
Stir in half the grated apple
Spoon into a bowl and top with the rest of the apple
Drizzle with honey and cinnamon, add butter if you like

name.en: Fried egg with grilled tomato and mushroom

en: 2 eggs
2 tomatoes, halved
5 mushrooms
1 tsp olive oil
Salt, black pepper, parsley
Grill the tomato and mushrooms in a pan with the oil 6 minutes
Fry the eggs in another pan until the white sets
Arrange it all on one plate
Season with salt, pepper and parsley
Ready-made whole-wheat crumpets, 2 pieces (80 g)
Low-fat butter 1 tsp
Honey 2 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon (optional)
Fresh berries to serve (optional)
A little salt
Toast the crumpets in a toaster or dry pan for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp on the outside.
Butter them immediately while hot so it melts evenly.
Drizzle the honey over them, letting it pool in the characteristic holes.
Sprinkle with cinnamon if desired, and serve with fresh berries immediately.

name.en: Kedgeree (Smoked Fish and Rice with Egg)

en: Smoked fish fillet (haddock or salmon) 100 g
Cooked basmati rice 150 g
2 boiled eggs, quartered
1 small chopped onion and mild curry powder half a tsp
Chopped parsley for garnish and a little lemon juice
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Poach the smoked fish in boiling water 6-8 minutes until cooked, drain and flake into large pieces.
Brown the onion in the oil, add the curry powder and stir for a minute.
Add the cooked rice and gently stir until it takes on the curry flavour.
Add the flaked fish and stir gently, arrange the egg quarters on top, garnish with parsley and lemon juice, and serve hot.

name.en: Turkey Bacon with Mushrooms and Tomatoes on Toast

en: Lean turkey bacon, 4 slices (50 g)
Sliced mushrooms 100 g
Cherry tomatoes, halved, 100 g
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g)
1 small crushed garlic clove and 1 tsp oil
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat, cook the turkey bacon 2-3 minutes per side until crisp, set aside.
Add the oil and garlic to the same pan, add the mushrooms and stir for 5 minutes until they soften and release their water.
Add the cherry tomatoes and stir 2-3 minutes until they soften slightly, adjust the salt and black pepper.
Toast the bread, arrange the mushrooms and tomatoes on top with the turkey bacon slices, garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Warm Grain Porridge with Dried Fruit

en: Mixed grains (oats and barley) 40 g
Low-fat milk 250 ml
Dried apricots and raisins, chopped, 30 g total
Honey 1 tsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Sliced almonds for garnish (optional)
Put the mixed grains and milk in a small pot.
Cook over low heat 10-12 minutes, stirring, until cooked and the texture becomes creamy.
Add the chopped apricots and raisins and cook 3 more minutes.
Pour into a serving bowl, add the honey, sprinkle with cinnamon and almonds, and serve warm.
2 eggs
2 slices whole-wheat bread (60 g)
Low-fat butter 1 tsp
Salt and black pepper
Place the eggs in boiling water and cook for exactly 6-7 minutes for a soft, runny centre.
Meanwhile, toast the bread slices and butter them.
Cut the toast into long thin strips (soldiers).
Place the eggs in egg cups, slice off the top, sprinkle with salt and black pepper, and serve immediately with the toast soldiers for dipping.

name.en: Bubble and Squeak (Potato and Cabbage Cakes)

en: Boiled, mashed potato 150 g
Boiled, chopped cabbage 100 g
1 small chopped onion
1 egg and 1 tbsp whole-wheat flour
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the mashed potato with the chopped cabbage, onion, egg, flour, salt and black pepper until well combined.
Shape the mixture into two flat patties with your hands.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp on the outside.
Smoked kipper fillet 140 g
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g)
A thin layer of low-fat butter
A little lemon juice and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Cherry tomatoes to serve (optional)
Place the kipper fillet on a lined tray.
Grill under the broiler 6-8 minutes until cooked and its surface flakes slightly.
Toast the bread and butter it.
Serve the kipper with the toast, drizzle with lemon juice and black pepper, garnish with parsley and cherry tomatoes if desired.

name.en: Scrambled Eggs with Smoked Salmon and Chives

en: 2 eggs
Smoked salmon, cut into strips, 40 g
Chopped chives 1 tbsp
Low-fat milk 1 tbsp
A little salt (the salmon is already salty) and black pepper
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g) to serve
Beat the eggs with the milk, a little salt and black pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat, pour in the beaten eggs.
Stir gently and constantly until the eggs begin to set, add the smoked salmon and two thirds of the chives.
Keep stirring 1-2 minutes until the eggs set but stay soft, sprinkle with the remaining chives and serve with the bread.

name.en: Jacket potato with beans and cheese

en: 1 large potato
Half cup white beans in a light tomato sauce
30 g grated low-fat cheddar
Chopped spring onion
Salt, black pepper
Prick the potato several times with a fork
Bake at 200°C for 50 minutes until the flesh is soft
Split it and top with the beans and cheese
Return for 5 minutes until the cheese melts, then top with spring onion
300 g frozen peas
1 small onion
2 cups vegetable stock
Fresh mint leaves
1 tsp oil, 1 tbsp yogurt
Sauté the onion in the oil 3 minutes
Add the stock, bring to a boil, then add the peas for 4 minutes
Blend the soup with the mint until smooth
Serve with a spoon of yogurt on top

name.en: Ploughman's Lunch Platter (Cheese, Bread and Pickle)

en: Low-fat cheddar cheese 50 g
Whole-wheat bread, 2 slices (60 g)
Small pickled onions or pickled cucumber 40 g
1 small apple, sliced
5 cherry tomatoes
Chutney 1 tbsp to serve
Arrange the cheese on a serving plate in chunks or slices.
Place the bread alongside.
Add the pickle, apple and cherry tomatoes distributed around the plate.
Serve with the chutney on the side for dipping.
Leek, sliced, 150 g
Potato, cubed, 150 g
1 small onion
Light vegetable stock 400 ml
1 tbsp light cream (optional)
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Brown the leek and onion in a dry pot for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the potato and vegetable stock, cover and simmer over medium heat 18-20 minutes until the potato is fully tender.
Blend the soup with an immersion blender until smooth.
Add the cream if desired, adjust the salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Cooked, chopped chicken breast 120 g
Leek, sliced, 100 g and carrot, chopped, 50 g
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp and low-fat milk 150 ml for the sauce
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (60 g)
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
1 beaten egg for brushing (optional)
Brown the leek and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the flour and stir for a minute, then gradually add the milk, stirring constantly, until the texture thickens without lumps.
Add the chopped chicken, salt and black pepper, pour the mixture into a small oven-safe dish.
Cover with the pastry sheet, prick the surface with a fork and brush with the egg if desired, bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until the pastry top is golden.
Boiled, chopped chicken breast 130 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp and low-fat mayonnaise 1 tbsp
Mild curry powder half a tsp and a little lemon juice
Raisins 1 tbsp and sliced almonds for garnish
Lettuce and cucumber to serve 100 g
Cooked basmati rice 80 g (optional) and salt
Mix the yogurt, mayonnaise, curry powder, lemon juice and salt to make the dressing.
Add the chopped boiled chicken and toss until evenly coated.
Add the raisins and stir gently.
Serve over the lettuce and cucumber, or with the rice, and sprinkle with almonds for garnish.
Lean minced beef 100 g
Potato, carrot and turnip, small cubes, 150 g total
1 small chopped onion
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (80 g)
Salt and black pepper
1 beaten egg for brushing
Mix the minced meat with the potato, carrot, turnip, onion, salt and black pepper.
Roll out the pastry into a circle, place the filling on one half.
Fold the other half over the filling and press the edges to seal, crimp the edge to form the characteristic pasty crest.
Brush with the egg, place on a lined tray, and bake at 190°C for 40-45 minutes until fully cooked and golden.
Cauliflower, cut into florets, 300 g
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Low-fat cheddar cheese, grated, 50 g
Mild mustard half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Fine breadcrumbs 1 tbsp for topping (optional)
Boil the cauliflower florets in salted water 5-6 minutes until slightly softened while keeping their texture, drain.
Dissolve the flour in a little cold milk, heat the remaining milk and gradually add the flour mixture, stirring, until the texture thickens.
Add half the cheese, mustard, salt and black pepper, mix until the cheese melts.
Place the cauliflower in a small oven-safe dish, pour the sauce over it, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and breadcrumbs if desired, and bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden on top.

name.en: Baked Jacket Potato with Tuna and Sweetcorn

en: 1 large potato (250 g)
Canned tuna in water, drained, 80 g
Cooked sweetcorn 40 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp
Chopped spring onion and a little lemon juice
Salt and black pepper
Prick the potato several times with a fork, bake at 200°C for 50-60 minutes until fully cooked and the skin turns crisp.
Mix the tuna with the sweetcorn, yogurt, spring onion, lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Cut the potato from the top and squeeze the sides to open it.
Stuff it with the tuna mixture and serve hot.
Lean lamb or beef, small cubes, 100 g
Pearl barley 40 g
Carrot, celery and turnip, chopped, 150 g total
1 medium onion
Light vegetable stock 500 ml and a bay leaf
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Brown the meat in a dry pot for 4 minutes until it changes colour.
Add the onion, carrot, celery and turnip and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the pearl barley, stock and bay leaf.
Cover and simmer 45-50 minutes until the meat is tender and the barley is cooked, adjust the salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
170 g salmon fillet
200 g frozen peas
1 tsp chopped mint
Juice of half a lemon
1 tsp olive oil, salt, pepper
Season the salmon with the oil, lemon and salt
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes
Boil the peas 4 minutes and mash with the mint
Serve the salmon on top of the mashed peas
150 g lean minced beef
2 medium potatoes, boiled and mashed
1 carrot and 1 onion, chopped
1 tsp tomato paste
Light beef stock, salt, pepper
Brown the meat with the onion and carrot 8 minutes
Add the tomato paste and half a cup of stock, cook 10 minutes
Put it in a baking dish and top with the mashed potato
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden on top

name.en: Baked Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy

en: Lean chicken or beef sausages, 4 pieces (140 g)
Boiled, mashed potato 200 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp for the mash
1 large onion, thinly sliced
Light vegetable stock 150 ml and cornflour 1 tsp for the gravy
Salt and black pepper
Arrange the sausages on a lined tray and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked.
Mash the boiled potato with the milk and salt until smooth.
Brown the onion in a dry pan for 8-10 minutes until dark golden and sweet, add the stock and dissolved cornflour and cook 3 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Serve the sausages over the mashed potato with the onion gravy.
White fish fillet (cod or haddock) 140 g
Coarse breadcrumbs 30 g, 1 egg and 1 tbsp flour
Potato, cut into thick sticks, 200 g
2 tsp oil for the potatoes and 1 tsp for the fish
Salt, black pepper and boiled peas to serve
Vinegar or lemon to serve (optional)
Toss the potato sticks with the oil and salt, arrange on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 15 minutes.
Coat the fish in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Add the fish to the tray with the potatoes and bake together 15-18 more minutes until the potatoes are golden and the fish flakes easily.
Serve with the boiled peas and vinegar or lemon.

name.en: Baked Toad in the Hole (Sausages in Yorkshire Pudding Batter)

en: Lean chicken or beef sausages, 4 pieces (140 g)
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
2 eggs
Low-fat milk 150 ml
1 tsp oil for the tin, salt and a pinch of black pepper
Chopped spring onion for garnish (optional)
Beat the eggs with the milk, gradually whisk in the flour until a smooth, lump-free batter forms, add salt and black pepper and let it rest 15 minutes.
Grease a small baking tin with oil and place the sausages in it, put it in an oven at 220°C for 5 minutes until the oil is well heated.
Quickly remove the tin and pour the egg batter directly over the hot sausages.
Return to the oven immediately and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the oven door until it puffs up and turns golden, garnish with spring onion if desired and serve immediately.

name.en: British Beef Stew with Root Vegetables

en: Lean beef, small cubes, 120 g
Carrot and turnip, chopped, 150 g total
Potato, cubed, 100 g
1 medium onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
A bay leaf and light vegetable stock 350 ml
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the beef and stir until it changes colour.
Add the carrot, turnip, potato, bay leaf and stock.
Cover and simmer 50-55 minutes until the beef is tender and the vegetables are cooked, adjust the salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Baked Lancashire Hotpot (Lamb and Potato Casserole)

en: Lean lamb or beef, small cubes, 120 g
Potato, thinly sliced, 200 g
1 large onion, sliced, and carrot, chopped, 50 g
Light vegetable stock 250 ml and a bay leaf
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil
Brown the meat in the oil for 4-5 minutes until it changes colour, set aside.
In the same pan, stir the onion and carrot for 3 minutes.

Layer the potato slices in the bottom of an oven-safe dish, then the meat, onion and carrot, then the remaining potato on top, add the bay leaf, salt and black pepper and pour in the stock until it covers the second-to-last layer.
Cover with foil and bake at 180°C for an hour and a quarter, then uncover and bake 15-20 more minutes until the top potato layer is golden.

name.en: Grilled Liver and Onions with Mash

en: Beef or chicken liver, sliced, 120 g
2 large onions, thinly sliced
1 tsp whole-wheat flour for coating
Boiled, mashed potato 200 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp for the mash
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Heat the oil and brown the onion for 10-12 minutes over medium heat until golden and sweet, set aside.
Coat the liver slices in the flour with salt and black pepper.
Cook the liver in the same pan for just 2-3 minutes per side until done without becoming tough.
Mash the boiled potato with the milk and salt, and serve the liver over it with the browned onion.

name.en: Light Baked Steak and Kidney Pie

en: Lean beef, small cubes, 100 g
Beef or lamb kidney, small cubes, 50 g
1 medium onion and mushrooms, chopped, 50 g
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp and light vegetable stock 200 ml
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (60 g)
Salt, black pepper and 1 beaten egg for brushing
Brown the beef and kidney in a dry pan for 5 minutes until they change colour.
Add the onion and mushrooms and stir for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the flour and stir for a minute, then gradually add the stock, stirring, until the texture thickens, adjust the salt and black pepper and simmer on low heat 15 minutes.
Pour the mixture into a small oven-safe dish, cover with the pastry sheet, prick with a fork and brush with the egg, bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until the pastry top is golden.

name.en: Roast Pork Chops with Apple Sauce

en: Lean pork or turkey chops 140 g
1 medium apple, peeled and chopped
1 tsp brown sugar and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Salt, black pepper and 1 crushed garlic clove
1 tsp oil
Steamed broccoli to serve 150 g
Season the chops with salt, black pepper and crushed garlic, let them sit 10 minutes.
Cook the chopped apple with the brown sugar, cinnamon and a little water in a small pot over medium heat 8-10 minutes until soft, mash slightly with a fork.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the chops 5-6 minutes per side until fully cooked.
Serve the meat with the apple sauce and steamed broccoli.
3 low-salt ready oatcakes
40 g low-fat cheddar
Apple or grape slices
A pinch of black pepper
Rocket leaves (optional)
Slice the cheese thinly
Lay it on the oatcakes
Add the fruit slices and rocket
Sprinkle with black pepper and serve at once
2 carrots, cut into sticks
Half cup boiled chickpeas
1 tsp tahini
Juice of half a lemon, 1 garlic clove
1 tsp olive oil, salt
Blend the chickpeas with tahini, garlic and lemon
Add the oil and salt, whip until creamy
Add a spoon of water if too thick
Serve with the carrot sticks
1 boiled, peeled egg
Lean minced chicken or turkey 80 g
Chopped spring onion and mild mustard half a tsp
Fine breadcrumbs 20 g and another beaten egg for coating
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Knead the minced meat with the spring onion, mustard, salt and black pepper.
Flatten the mixture on your wet palm, place the boiled egg in the centre and wrap it to cover completely.
Coat in the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with oil, bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden on the outside.
Whole-wheat bread, 2 slices (60 g)
Low-fat cheddar cheese, sliced, 40 g
Chutney 1 tbsp
1 lettuce leaf
Thinly sliced tomato
A thin layer of low-fat butter (optional)
Butter the bread slice if desired.
Spread the chutney over it in a thin layer.
Arrange the cheese, lettuce and tomato on top.
Cover with the other slice, cut in half and serve.
1 slice whole-wheat bread (40 g)
Low-fat cheddar cheese, grated, 40 g
Mild mustard half a tsp
1 tbsp low-fat milk
A few drops of low-sodium Worcestershire sauce (optional)
Black pepper
Toast the bread slice until lightly golden.
Mix the grated cheese with the mustard, milk, Worcestershire sauce and black pepper until combined.
Spread the mixture over the toasted bread in a thick layer.
Place under the broiler 3-4 minutes until the cheese melts and turns bubbly golden, and serve immediately.
Lean minced chicken or turkey 100 g
1 small finely chopped onion and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Mixed dried herbs half a tsp, salt and black pepper
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (50 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing
Sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Knead the minced meat with the onion, garlic, herbs, salt and black pepper.
Roll out the pastry, place the meat mixture in a long cylinder along one edge, roll tightly.
Cut the cylinder into 4 equal pieces.
Arrange on a lined tray, brush with the egg, sprinkle with sesame if desired, and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Low-fat cheddar cheese, grated, 50 g
Cold low-fat butter 2 tsp
About 2 tbsp cold water
A little salt and a pinch of paprika (optional)
A pinch of fennel or caraway seeds (optional)
Mix the flour with the grated cheese, salt and paprika.
Add the cold butter and rub it into the flour with fingertips until the texture resembles crumbs.
Gradually add the cold water and knead quickly until a cohesive dough forms.
Roll it out and cut into long thin strips, sprinkle with fennel seeds if desired, and bake at 190°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and crisp.
1 whole-wheat English muffin (60 g)
Lean turkey bacon, 2 slices (25 g)
1 egg
A thin slice of low-fat cheddar cheese (optional)
Salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil
Split the muffin in half and toast it in a toaster or dry pan until golden.
Heat the oil and cook the turkey bacon 2-3 minutes per side until crisp, set aside.
In the same pan, cook the egg fried or poached as desired, season with salt and black pepper.
Assemble the bacon, egg and cheese if desired between the muffin halves, and serve hot.
Lean minced pork or turkey 100 g
1 small finely chopped onion and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Dried marjoram half a tsp, salt and black pepper
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (70 g)
1 beaten egg for brushing
Mild mustard to serve (optional)
Knead the minced meat with the onion, garlic, marjoram, salt and black pepper.
Cut the pastry into two medium circles, place the filling in the centre of each.
Gather the edges toward the centre and press to seal, flip so the sealed side is down.
Brush with the egg, arrange on a lined tray, and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until fully cooked and golden, serve with mustard if desired.
Skinless chicken drumsticks, 3 pieces (250 g)
2 crushed garlic cloves and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Mixed dried herbs (thyme and rosemary) 1 tsp
1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Mix the crushed garlic with the lemon juice, dried herbs, oil, salt and black pepper.
Rub the chicken drumsticks thoroughly with the mixture and let them sit at least 20 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden on the outside, garnish with parsley if desired.
150 g strawberries, chopped
150 g Greek yogurt
1 small meringue nest, crushed
1 tsp honey
Mint leaves to garnish
Mash half the strawberries, leave the rest in pieces
Mix the yogurt with the honey
Layer yogurt, strawberries and meringue alternately in a glass
Garnish with a mint leaf and serve at once
1 ripe pear, halved
A pinch of ground ginger
1 tsp honey
A small knob of butter
1 tbsp crunchy oats
Scoop out a little of the pear's core with a spoon
Drizzle the ginger and honey over it
Put the butter into the hollow
Bake 20 minutes and scatter the oats before serving
Pitted, chopped dates 100 g
Hot water 80 ml and baking soda half a tsp
Whole-wheat flour 50 g and baking powder half a tsp
1 egg and 1 tsp oil
Brown sugar 2 tsp for the sauce and water 2 tbsp
1 tsp low-fat butter for the sauce
Pour the hot water over the chopped dates with the baking soda, let the mixture sit 10 minutes until the dates soften.
Mash the dates slightly with a fork, add the egg and oil and mix.
Add the flour and baking powder and mix gently until combined, pour into a small greased tin.
Bake at 180°C for 20-22 minutes until cooked. For the sauce, melt the brown sugar, butter and water in a small pan 2-3 minutes, pour over the warm pudding before serving.
Whole-wheat bread, 3 slices (90 g)
A thin layer of low-fat butter for spreading
Raisins 1 tbsp
1 egg and low-fat milk 150 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Vanilla extract half a tsp
Spread the bread slices with butter, cut into triangles.
Arrange them overlapping in a small oven-safe dish, distributing the raisins between them.
Beat the egg with the milk, brown sugar, cinnamon and vanilla, pour over the bread and let it sit 10 minutes to soak in.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until set and golden on top, and serve warm.
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (50 g)
Date syrup or black treacle 70 g
Fine breadcrumbs 30 g
Grated lemon zest and lemon juice 1 tsp
1 small beaten egg
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Line a small greased tart tin with the pastry, prick the base with a fork.
Mix the treacle with the breadcrumbs, lemon zest, lemon juice, egg and cinnamon until combined.
Pour the mixture evenly over the pastry.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the filling sets and the pastry turns golden, let cool slightly before serving.
Thin whole-wheat bread, 4 slices (120 g)
Mixed fresh or frozen berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries) 300 g
Brown sugar 30 g
Water 2 tbsp
Lemon juice 1 tsp
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Cook the berries with the brown sugar, water and lemon juice over medium heat 5-7 minutes until they soften and release their juice, let the mixture cool slightly.
Trim the crusts off the bread, line a small mould (cup or bowl) with the bread slices, leaving some for the top.
Pour the cooked berries with their juice into the mould, cover with the remaining bread slices.
Place a light weight on top and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight, invert onto a serving plate and garnish with mint before serving.

name.en: Light Baked Spotted Dick (Currant Sponge Pudding)

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Currants or raisins 40 g
1 egg
Low-fat milk 60 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp and grated lemon zest
Baking powder half a tsp and 1 tsp oil for the tin
Beat the egg with the brown sugar and lemon zest until the mixture becomes pale.
Add the milk and mix, then gradually add the flour and baking powder until a smooth batter forms.
Add the currants and mix gently.
Pour into a small tin greased with oil, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until cooked and it springs back when pressed gently, let cool slightly before slicing.
1 sheet thin whole-wheat pastry (60 g)
Currants or raisins 50 g
Brown sugar 2 tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
A little grated orange zest
Egg white for brushing
A little coarse sugar for garnish (optional)
Mix the currants with the brown sugar, cinnamon and orange zest.
Cut the pastry into two medium circles.
Place the filling in the centre of each circle, gather the edges toward the centre and press to seal, flip so the sealed side is down.
Gently flatten with your hand slightly, make 3 small slits on top, brush with the egg white and sprinkle with coarse sugar if desired, and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
2 eggs
Brown sugar 30 g
Low-fat Greek yogurt 2 tbsp
Baking powder half a tsp
Low-sugar strawberry jam 2 tbsp for the filling
Beat the eggs with the brown sugar using an electric whisk for 4-5 minutes until the mixture becomes pale and thick.
Add the yogurt and mix gently, then gradually fold in the flour and baking powder until combined without deflating the mixture.
Divide the batter between two small greased tins, bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked and they spring back when pressed gently.
Let them cool completely, spread the jam on one and place the other on top to form the cake.
Whole-wheat flour 70 g
Baking powder half a tsp and a pinch of salt
Low-fat milk 50 ml and 1 tsp oil
Low-sugar strawberry or apricot jam 40 g
A little grated lemon zest (optional)
A light dusting of icing sugar for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, gradually add the milk and oil until a soft, non-sticky dough forms.
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface into a thin rectangle.
Spread the jam evenly over it, leaving a small border, sprinkle with lemon zest if desired, and roll it up tightly from the long edge.
Place on a lined tray with the seam facing down, bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes until golden, let cool slightly, slice and dust lightly with icing sugar if desired.
